home.faq.q1: Do learners have to know English?
home.faq.a1: No. Professor Qubirex teaches in Telugu or Hindi, by voice or text. Technical words stay in English, explained in your language, because that is how they appear at work.
home.faq.a2: Nothing. Learners join free through their college. Colleges and employers pay for what they use — talk to us for pricing.
home.faq.a3: By passing fresh checks written by the assessment system, not the teacher, spread over time. The Passport shows how each skill was checked and how sure we are the learner did the work.
home.faq.q4: Who can see a learner’s details?
home.faq.a4: Anyone can check that a Passport is genuine. The skills and evidence go to an employer only after the learner says yes. Colleges see progress, never session conversations.
home.faq.q5: Can I try it without signing up?
home.faq.a5: Yes. The live demo shows each side with sample data. Nothing you do there is saved.

lj.home.nextWhy.dayone: A short work-like task. Employers see how you do on day one.
lj.home.nextWhy.application: See where your application is and what happens next.
lj.home.nextWhy.keep_fresh: Short reviews keep your labels from fading.
lj.home.nextWhy.renew: Some skills need a refresh. A review takes about 2 minutes.
lj.home.why: Qubirex picks the one step that moves you forward most, from where you are now: your lessons, checks, reviews and employer requests.
lj.home.measures: Skills done counts skills where you passed the check. How well you know them is the average score of those checks.
lj.today.practise: Your college asked you to practise {skills} before {date}
lj.today.reviewWhy: Reviews keep a skill fresh on your Passport. If you skip them, the skill shows as Needs refresh and can drop from Confirmed.
lj.record.avgExplain: The average score of the checks you passed.
lj.record.timeExplain: Time spent in lessons and checks. Idle time is not counted.
lj.plan.add: + Add this skill to my plan
lj.jobs.twoWaysTitle: Found by employers, or asked directly
lj.jobs.twoWays: When you let employers find you, verified employers see your Confirmed skills and city in their search, without your name. Separately, any employer can ask you directly to see your Passport. Either way, nothing more is shared until you say yes.
lj.jobs.discoverableOffDone: Employers can no longer find you in search.
lj.jobs.outsideNote: These posts are on other sites. Apply there, then mark it here so you can keep track.
lj.passport.provesTitle: What this Passport proves, and what it doesn't
lj.passport.proves1: You answered checks on these skills yourself, on the dates shown.
lj.passport.proves2: Confirmed skills were shown in two different ways, over time.
lj.passport.proves3: The facts are signed, so anyone can check them with your Evidence ID.
lj.passport.doesNot2: How fast you learned, or how many tries it took. That is never shown.
lj.passport.doesNot3: A grade or a rank against other students.
lj.passport.viewsWhy: Counts from the last 90 days. Employers count when you let them see your skills; public counts when someone opens your shared link.
lj.passport.noViews: No one has viewed it in the last 90 days.
lj.passport.changedSinceShare: Your labels changed since you shared on {date}. Your shared link always shows today's labels.
lj.passport.todayLabels: Your shared link always shows today's labels.
lj.passport.renewSoon: Your Passport ends on {date}. Renew it with one short question per skill.
lj.resume.claimsTitle: Your résumé vs what is proven
lj.resume.claimsHow: Paste the skills line from your résumé. We show which ones Qubirex has seen you prove.
lj.resume.missingOnResume: Proven but missing from your résumé: {list}
lj.reviews.why: We forget what we don't use. A short question at the right time keeps a skill in memory, and each review is a dated fact on your Passport.
lj.reviews.skip: Nothing is taken away, but the skill starts to show as Ageing, then Needs refresh. A Confirmed skill that goes stale drops to Partial until you review it again.
lj.settings.deleteHow: We email you a 6-digit code to confirm. Your account is then deleted after 14 days; you can cancel any time before that.
lj.settings.codeSentTo: We sent a code to {to}. It works for 15 minutes.
lj.settings.codeSent: Your college has your contact. Ask them for the code, or add an email to your profile.
lj.settings.deleteScheduled: Your account will be deleted on {date}. Your Passport stops working then. Until that day you can keep your account.
lj.welcome.sub: Three short steps, then you start learning.
lj.welcome.micHow: Tap the mic and say {prompt}. We listen for {s} seconds.
lj.welcome.noMic: No microphone here? That's fine: you can type every answer.
lj.welcome.checkWhy: About 10 minutes of short questions. It finds what you already know, so your path skips it. It is not a test you can fail.
lj.welcome.profileLater: Your education, projects and goals can wait.

lj.inst.helpNone: No student is waiting for help.
lj.inst.replyHint: A hint, an example, or when to meet
lj.emp.shortlistedDone: Shortlisted. The student has been told.
lj.emp.noTries: Tries that did not pass and time taken are never shown.
lj.emp.labelsNotShared: The student did not share labels.
lj.emp.cameraOn: Camera on (the student confirmed it) · away from the page {s}s
voice.issue.busy: Professor Qubirex's voice is busy right now, so this one is shown as text. The next reply will be spoken again.
voice.issue.tap: Your browser paused the voice. Tap Replay to hear it.
voice.issue.none: Professor Qubirex's voice is not available on this deployment, so replies show as text.
voice.issue.text: High-quality voice is not available right now — reading the lesson as text.
voice.deviceChoiceHelp: Only when Professor Qubirex's voice is not available. Phone voices can sound robotic in Telugu and Hindi.
lj.courses.title: Topics
lj.courses.sub: Each topic is its own course, in a clear order: Module 1, Lesson 1, then the next.
lj.courses.programmeSub: The path your college set. It stays required.
lj.courses.exploreSub: Pick only what you want to learn. Already know a lesson? Test out of it.
lj.courses.draftsSub: These courses are drafted and need faculty review before they open fully.
lj.courses.draftNote: Draft — needs faculty review. The order is set; lessons are still being written.
lj.course.moduleEnd: Pass the test and the project to add this skill group to your Passport.
lj.home.topicsEmpty: Pick a topic to learn alongside your college programme, like Python or Java.
lj.module.testSub: Pass {pass} of {of} to complete the test.
lj.module.testNotYet: {score} of {of}. You need {needed}. Read the reasons below and try again.
lj.module.projectNotYet: Some tests did not pass yet. Fix them and run again.
lj.module.completed: Module complete: this skill group is now on your Passport.
lj.lesson.notInLanguage: This lesson is not ready in {lang} yet.
lj.lesson.availableIn: Available in {list} for now. Change the learning language above.
lj.lesson.suggestPrev: This lesson builds on the one before. Learn it first?
lj.lesson.timedOut: The code ran too long and was stopped. Look for a loop that never ends.
lj.lesson.javaPending: Java runs on our server soon. For now, Java answers are checked by their structure, and the example shows its known output.
lj.lesson.testsInfo: {shown} tests you can see, {hidden} hidden tests
lj.lesson.hiddenFailed: A hidden test did not pass. Try other values, like zero or a negative number.
lj.lesson.allPassed: All tests passed. Well done — the check is open.
lj.lesson.notYet: Not yet. Read what failed, fix it and run again.
lj.lesson.checkEarly: You can take the check now; if it does not go well, the lesson is here.
lj.lesson.checkWhy: A fresh question about this lesson. Answer in your own words, by voice or typing.
lj.lesson.earlyNote: you can try now; we'll explain again if needed
lj.lesson.challengeWhy: Say it aloud in your own words. A spoken answer shows the work is yours and makes the skill stronger on your Passport.
lj.lesson.challengePassed: Spoken challenge passed. This lesson is now {label}.
lj.lesson.challengeAgain: Not yet. Try again, and use the key words from the lesson.
lj.lesson.askHint: For example: Why do we use return? · Explain in Telugu · Slower · Another example
lj.lesson.clearThanks: Thank you. Your professor sees this.
lj.lesson.testoutWhy: Answer both questions. If they pass, this lesson is marked Known and skipped; the evidence goes on your Passport like any check.
lj.lesson.testoutKnown: Passed. This lesson is marked Known.
lj.lesson.testoutLearn: Not yet — let's learn it from here.
inst.topics.title: Topics
inst.topics.sub: Every course your students can learn: modules, lessons, hours and how they are checked. Read any lesson in English, Telugu or Hindi, mark it Reviewed or suggest an edit.
inst.topics.checkedBy: Students are checked by: practice code run against tests, a fresh check question each attempt, a spoken challenge, a module test and a module project.
inst.topics.markedReviewed: Marked Reviewed. Your students now see "Reviewed by your faculty" on this lesson.
inst.topics.suggestLabel: Suggest an edit (what to change and why)
inst.topics.suggestionSent: Suggestion sent to the Qubirex content team.
inst.topics.noFeedback: No feedback on this lesson yet.
inst.topics.programmeNote: To build a programme from these modules, start a new cohort and list the modules in its brief.
inst.students.extraNotShared: The student has not chosen to share their own topics with the college.
pub.topics.title: See our topics
pub.topics.sub: Every course is taught first, then practised with real code, then checked. Try one free lesson from each course, in English, Telugu or Hindi.
pub.topics.howChecked: Checks: practice code run against tests, a fresh question each attempt, a spoken challenge, module tests and projects. Passing a module adds that skill group to the learner's Passport.
pub.topics.sampleMissing: This lesson is not a free sample.
pub.topics.moreText: Sign in to practise with real code, take the checks and earn Passport skills.
demo2.story.topicsText: Open Topics, read a Python lesson in Telugu and mark it Reviewed; your students then see "Reviewed by your faculty"
